selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).
remaining: whether a recovery whose slow quorum contains the differing peer rather than the committed leader re-proposes the peer's smaller vector for the instance (the highest-vbal selection cannot separate them because both records carry the pre-accept ballot as vbal) (S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether the already-committed leader then refuses the later Commit and keeps the larger vector, freezing two committed vectors for one instance (handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED) (S13-handleCommit)
whether the two vectors order conflicting instances differently, since the difference is a dependency component on a row whose conflicting command may not yet be committed at the peer (S20-exec)

whether the recovery-led fast commit is reachable with a single peer reply inside the exempted configuration, that is whether an N=3 deployment with a non-owner recovery is a supported history (S24-runReplica-epaxos, S21-quorum-sizes)
feedback.rationale: This refines, rather than replaces, the earlier correction: the merged vector is what gets committed, and the question is whether any other replica holds it at the same vbal. The owner-led case is now explained (a single peer's vector dominates and is adopted by both), which is consistent with the source comment that equality need not be checked there. The recovery-led case remains open and is the discriminator a controlled schedule would settle; recording it here keeps the map stable and leaves the Candidate's proposition intact while making the next construction step concrete. Nothing in the requirement, the observed behaviors or the previously explained Candidate is weakened.

selections.rationale: Sourced review answers the Candidate's discriminator instead of leaving it open. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given, starting from the deps vector carried in the message and skipping the row of the instance owner named in that message, so a pre-accepting peer returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise. With one counted peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's componentwise merge therefore equals that peer's vector in every compared component, and mergeAttributes ignores only the leader's own row. In an owner-led instance the peer skips exactly that row, so the merged vector equals the peer's record and the fast-commit branch installs the same vector on the leader: both members of the fast quorum hold the committed vector at the same vbal, and any recovery quorum the recoverer can assemble (self plus one reply, with both remaining replicas being fast-quorum members) contains a holder. That mechanism is what keeps the exemption from publishing an unsupported vector, so the proposition is explained. The surviving exposure is confined to one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes keeps the leader's own row value while the peer may have raised it; it requires the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader, and it is recorded as the remaining premise. The map is updated in the same product (B4's unknown and the N<=3 open detail) so the earlier, over-broad phrasing does not mislead the next question.

feedback.answered: The exemption's exposure is resolved for the reachable owner-led case. updateAttributes starts from the deps vector carried by the message, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and only raises components from local conflict knowledge, so the peer's reply vector dominates the leader's (S7-attributes). mergeAttributes raises every component except the leader's own row (S10-handlePreAcceptReply), so with exactly one counted peer the committed merged vector equals the peer's record in every compared component; for an owner-led instance the peer skips exactly the row mergeAttributes ignores, hence peer and leader records coincide, the leader's fast-commit branch installs the same vector, both fast-quorum members hold the committed vector at the same vbal, and every recovery quorum the recoverer can assemble (its own reply plus one of the other two replicas, both fast-quorum members) contains a holder (S15-handlePrepareReply). The source comment that equality need not be checked for N <= 3 with Thrifty therefore has a concrete mechanism in this case, and the earlier reading that the committed vector may be held only by the leader is not established for a live owner.
remaining: whether a recovery-led phase 1 (LeaderId != owner) can hand the peer a higher value for the leader's own dependency row than the leader holds, which is the one component mergeAttributes refuses to take from a reply (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether that gap requires a recovery leader that lost its conflict index, that is a restart under the launched configuration (Durable false, no stable-store reader) (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos)

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The exposed premise is therefore whether any replica other than the leader holds the merged vector at the instance's vbal, since the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes, S15-handlePrepareReply).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

selections.rationale: The frontier is without an open Candidate and the two recovery reachability questions are disposed, so this product opens the next one on the premise carried forward by the last two products: the accept phase stores accepted attributes without recording an accepted status. handleAccept writes Deps, Seq, bal and vbal and leaves Status at whatever it was (NONE for a record created by the Accept, PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ when the peer had already replied to the PreAccept), while three places in the code expect an acceptor's accepted status to be observable: handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard exists to avoid regressing accepted attributes, findPreAcceptConflicts' shortcut treats Status >= ACCEPTED as fixed, and handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 is defined by lb.status == ACCEPTED. The question is therefore whether any decision actually depends on that status, and in particular whether an accepted record can have its attributes recomputed afterwards or whether a recovery that should re-accept an accepted value instead restarts phase 1.

feedback.answered: The two reachability questions carried from the previous products are disposed: the TryPreAccept machinery is unreachable dead code (identical guards for sub-cases 3 and 4, and bcastTryPreAccept's only call site is the dead sub-case), so findPreAcceptConflicts' Status >= ACCEPTED shortcut and the possibleQuorum counting error cannot affect any decision; and the N <= 3 Thrifty equality exemption is explained for an owner-led instance by the dominance structure of updateAttributes plus mergeAttributes' row exception.
remaining: whether an accept-only acceptor (accept quorum member that never received the PreAccept) can have its accepted attributes recomputed by a later PreAccept, since handlePreAccept's guard cannot see the acceptance (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept)
whether that missing status changes which value a recovery re-proposes, because an accept-only acceptor reports the accepted vbal together with Status NONE and no command (S15-handlePrepareReply)
whether the residual recovery-led row-component gap of the N <= 3 exemption needs a restarted leader to become reachable (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos)
feedback.rationale: The new Candidate is grounded in a sourced discrepancy inside the slow path and is kept to one responsibility: the acceptor's record of an accepted value. Its supporting behaviours are named so the guards and the recovery dispatch that presuppose the status stay visible, and the counterevidence already excludes the one status shortcut that is unreachable, so the open question is specifically about accept-only acceptors and recovery. No map object is changed by this product, so the map's B5 unknown continues to describe the same premise at the level recorded there.

selections.rationale: Reading the recovery entry while working the accept-status premise produced a separate, sharper lead that belongs to its own question: startRecoveryForInstance raises the recovering replica's own vbal to the newly made ballot before building the self PrepareReply, so the self entry reports the new ballot as its VBallot while lb.ballot was seeded with the old vbal. Inside handlePrepareReply the selection rule is element.VBallot >= lb.ballot with lb.ballot updated as the loop runs, so the self entry raises the running ballot to the new one and every remote reply whose vbal is below the new ballot is then skipped. This product opens that as the next Candidate, keeps the accept-status Candidate open, and records no map change so the map basis stays stable.

feedback.answered: The accept-status Candidate's counterevidence is now sharper: the leader-side accept branch records ACCEPTED together with the merged attributes, so recovery sub-case 2 can be reached through a recovering replica's own record, while an accept-only acceptor reports accepted attributes with Status NONE and no command. While tracing that, the recovery entry's own vbal handling surfaced as a separate mechanism: the recovering replica reports the newly made ballot as its VBallot, which under the element.VBallot >= lb.ballot comparison can place the running maximum above every remote value at an older vbal.

selections.rationale: Construction run for the active recovery-vbal Candidate. The harness builds two real Replica values (a recovering replica holding only a default record for instance (1,0), and a peer whose record for the same instance is COMMITTED with a real PUT command), wires SendMsg through per-peer buffers, and delivers the messages through the real Marshal/Unmarshal form into the real handlers. It then reports (a) what the recovering replica reports as its own VBallot in the self PrepareReply, and (b) whether the remote COMMITTED reply is adopted or the resolution restarts phase 1. A local clean-copy run already showed the expected shape (self VBallot = the new ballot 3 while the seed lb.ballot is -1; the remote COMMITTED reply at vbal 0 is skipped; the instance ends PREACCEPTED with a NOOP command and a PreAccept is emitted), but that run is construction knowledge only; this product asks the trusted runner to reproduce the same events in a clean copy so the observation can be retained and used for a formal check.

The exploration submitted last turn was executed by the trusted runner in a clean copy and reproduced the same events as the local construction run, so the observed behaviour can now be recorded as construction knowledge with an execution reference. This product explains that execution, states precisely what it does and does not establish, and keeps the derived consequence as the next discriminator instead of treating it as a result. No map object is changed, so the map basis stays at version 4.

feedback.answered: In a clean copy the harness reported: recovery_seed with seed_lb_ballot -1, record_vbal_reported_by_self 3 and instance_vbal_after_seed 3 (so the self PrepareReply announces the newly made ballot, not the record's old vbal, and self_status is NONE); reply_delivered with prepare_replies 2 after the peer's real PrepareReply was pushed through the real wire form; and resolution with lb_status 1 (PREACCEPTED), instance_status 1 (PREACCEPTED), instance_cmds_len 1 with first op 0 (NOOP), adopted_committed_vector false, preaccept_sent true and out_codes starting with the PreAccept code 11. The final event records remote_status 4 (COMMITTED), instance_status_after 1 and command_after 0. So the mechanism is reproduced end to end on the trusted runner: a recovering replica holding only a default record ignores a PrepareReply that reports the instance COMMITTED at an older vbal and restarts phase 1 with NOOP, while the sender's own VBallot equals the new ballot and the leader bookkeeping was seeded with the old vbal.

whether that makes the effect a blocked catch-up (the recovering replica's row never advances, so its state machine freezes at the missing instance) rather than a divergence, which is the distinction that decides the importance of this finding

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. feedback.answered: Two premises that shaped this Candidate are settled. findPreAcceptConflicts' Status >= ACCEPTED shortcut cannot matter because its only caller is the unreachable TryPreAccept path, and recovery sub-case 2 can be reached only through the record of a replica that led the instance (the leader-side accept branch is the one place that stores ACCEPTED with the merged attributes), so an accept-only acceptor never reports an accepted status. Independently, the trusted checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed that the recovery value selection can end in a NOOP vector when it does not adopt a value another replica holds, which is the same outcome shape an accept-only acceptor's command-less reply would produce.

feedback.answered: The observable part of this Candidate resolves negatively. In handlePrepareReply the running maximum is seeded from the record's old vbal and immediately raised to the newly made ballot by the recovering replica's own entry (startRecoveryForInstance assigns inst.vbal = lastTriedBallot before building that reply), so every reply that holds a value at an older vbal - including an accept-only acceptor's command-less record at the accepted vbal - fails the element.VBallot >= lb.ballot test and is skipped. The command-less accept-only reply therefore cannot be preferred over an equal-vbal reply that carries the value, and the outcome shape is instead produced by the sibling mechanism already confirmed for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector: the recovery ignores all older-vbal replies and can commit a vector that no other replica holds. The other status consumer is dead code, and recovery sub-case 2 needs a replica whose own record is ACCEPTED, which only the leader-side accept branch produces.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

The recovery side is already confirmed (claim C1) and its applied effect is confirmed (claim C3), so the remaining unexplored consequence is the client contract: the proposal lived only on the original leader, the re-propose branch is guarded to the committing replica's own row, and replies are produced at execution under the launched configuration. feedback.answered: The client-side half of the question is answered on sources: the captured client has no retry and no reply deadline. SendProposal writes each proposal once (to the leader, or to the closest replica in the leaderless EPaxos configuration of run.go) and never re-sends it (S29-client-sendproposal). The reply path is a blocking read: WaitReplies loops on GetReplyFrom(waitFrom) and only leaves the loop when the read returns an error such as net.ErrClosed, at which point it logs and stops rather than re-sending (S28-client-waitreplies, S30-client-getreplyfrom). There is no timeout, no outstanding-request table and no CommandId-based retransmission, so a proposal whose instance was committed as NOOP by a recovery is never completed on either side: the recovering replica never held the proposals (it preserves only its own record's clientProposals), the re-propose branch requires the commit to land on the committing replica's own row with a single NONE command (S13-handleCommit), and the client does not re-issue the request.
remaining: whether the replica side could be expected to complete another replica's proposal, i.e. whether the recovering replica should adopt the owner's proposals when it recovers the owner's row (no read path does)

scope.description: Recovery decision for a single instance on the captured snapshot: N=3 with Thrifty and IsLeader false, the recovering replica holding only a default NONE record, one peer holding a COMMITTED record with a real command, and no third replica reply required.
assumptions: the recovering replica's own record carries no commands
a slow quorum (its own entry plus one reply) is sufficient to resolve
messages are delivered through the real wire format
excluded: producing the committed record through a real proposal, accept round and commit broadcast
execution of the instance and client-visible replies
configurations with N>3 or a live leader flag

blockers: Direct oracle correspondence remains disputed: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted; the plan's observable property asserts adopted_committed on the resolution event, and the harness prints instance_status and command_after in the same event, so the assertion is checkable against the raw fields rather than only through the derived boolean. Entry and caller duties: the recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance instead of the executeCommands timeout, and the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared rather than produced by a proposal and commit round; both substitutions are declared in the claim's scope and in the harness legality, and neither is needed for the resolution step the claim is about, because the resolution reads only the record, the reply slice and the running ballot. Oracle: adopted_committed is computed by the harness as an OR of two status fields, and the same event carries the status the code actually stored, so a change in the protocol's status semantics would show up in instance_status as well. Identity: the prerequisite and the resolution event share instance 1.0, which is the instance the harness seeds and drives, so correlation is non-trivial and monotone; the identity is written by the harness rather than read from the record, which is noted as a limitation rather than a defect because the harness constructs exactly one instance. Legal history: the prepared COMMITTED record corresponds to a state some history produced, but the trigger path is substituted, so the item is scoped to the resolution decision. Observation path and completion: all handlers are synchronous in the harness, the resolution is observed after handlePrepareReply returns, and the emitted message code is retained, so no wait or join is implied. Counterevidence: the alternative reading (the local record's new ballot legitimately outranks an older committed vbal) is recorded in the claim grounding and is not settled by this check; the item therefore does not promote the finding beyond the reviewed correspondence of predicate and observation. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the two reservations I hold are explained rather than hidden. First, the trigger (executeCommands timeout) and the production of the committed record are substituted, which limits the claim to the resolution decision; second, an alternative reading is that a recovering replica is only required to adopt the value with the highest vbal and that its own newly made ballot legitimately outranks an older committed ballot. I judge the alternative untenable because vbal records the ballot at which a value was accepted, while the recovering replica's fresh ballot carries no accepted value, and because the ignored reply reports COMMITTED, which is the one status the protocol treats as final; the check therefore corresponds to the written obligation, and the reservation is recorded so a later review can challenge it on sources rather than being surprised by it.

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicates: the obligation is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED is adopted; the first property asserts adopted_committed on the resolution event, and the second asserts vectors_match on the outcome event, which is the agreement form of the same requirement for the accept path. Both predicates are read from fields the harness prints together with the raw status, command and accept count, and the run reproduced adopted_committed false and vectors_match false with recoverer_command NONE against peer_committed_command PUT and accept_oks 1. Entry, schedule and completion: the harness drives Prepare/PrepareReply, the phase-1 restart's PreAccept/PreAcceptReply and the resulting Accept/AcceptReply in order, re-reading InstanceSpace after every delivery because startPhase1 replaces the record object, so the accept count that moves 0 to 1 and the COMMITTED status are read from the record the handlers actually wrote; the earlier mismatch (accept count read during the phase-1 reply, Accept never delivered) is fixed and the trailing diagnostic shows the Commit the recoverer broadcast. Oracle: vectors_match is the conjunction of the recoverer having committed and its command equalling the peer's, which is exactly the agreement question for one instance; the identity fields correlate the prerequisite reply and the outcome through the instance, not through the compared values. Legality: the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared rather than produced by a proposal round and the trigger is substituted, both declared in the claim scope; the rounds under test are the real handlers. Counterevidence and alternatives: the remaining reservations are that the property passes vacuously when the recoverer does not commit, that the propagation of the recoverer's Commit to other replicas is not driven, and that the alternative reading (a fresh ballot may legitimately outrank an older committed vbal) is answered for this path because the recoverer ends committed with a different command for an instance another replica already committed, which is the disagreement itself.

items.report_answer: 在被驱动的完整恢复路径上，已提交副本报告 COMMITTED(PUT) 时恢复者仍以 NOOP 重启阶段一并完成接受轮（accept_oks 0→1），最终自己提交 COMMITTED(NOOP)：vectors_match=false，即同一实例出现两个不同的已提交命令向量。该观察覆盖本轮驱动的全部轮次与最终记录，超出该路径的后果（其它副本的提交传播、客户端可见性）不在本次检查范围内。
limitations: the outcome property is a conditional: if the recoverer never commits, vectors_match is true and the property would hold vacuously; the outcome event prints recoverer_committed so the applicability is visible
the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared and the recovery is entered directly, so this check fixes the resolution and accept rounds, not the history that produced the commit
the recoverer's Commit propagation to the other replicas and any client-visible effect are not driven
the first property's review for the earlier artifact remains valid; this review covers the corrected artifact and its re-execution

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicates: the obligation is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED is adopted; the three properties encode its resolution form (adopted_committed), its two-record agreement form (vectors_match) and now its cluster form (all_committed_match) after the recoverer's Commit broadcast. Each predicate is read together with the raw fields the harness prints (status, per-replica command, accept count), and the retained stream shows replica0 NONE, replica1 PUT, replica2 NONE with all_committed_match false. Entry and schedule: the Commit is produced by the real bcastCommit inside handleAcceptReply, and it is delivered through the real wire form to the already-committed replica, where handleCommit returns early because the status is already COMMITTED, and to the third replica, which installs the command as a legal receiver would; the third replica's absence during the earlier rounds is a harness schedule choice, not a protocol assumption. Oracle: the property compares the committed command of each replica for one instance and identity field, which is the agreement question itself; the comparison is not derived from a context expected to change. Legal history: the already-committed record is a prepared state, so the check fixes the recovery rounds and the propagation, and treats a replica's COMMITTED record as the protocol's own evidence of a chosen value, which is how a PrepareReply with status COMMITTED is treated in the resolution under review. Observation path and completion: every handler is synchronous, the event is emitted after both deliveries, and the trailing diagnostic shows the messages the recoverer emitted, so no wait, join or cleanup duty is implied. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the reservations I hold are recorded as limitations rather than suppressed, namely that the committed records are prepared rather than produced by a proposal round, that the third property is an internal-record statement because the state machines are not executed, and that a reader who rejects the prepared COMMITTED record as evidence of a chosen value would also have to reject the protocol's own use of that status in the resolution.
items.report_title: 提交广播后同一实例出现两个已提交命令
items.report_answer: 恢复者以 NOOP 完成接受轮并提交后，其 Commit 广播被投递到已提交副本与从未见过该实例的第三副本：replica0 与 replica2 为 NONE，replica1 仍为 PUT（已提交副本因状态已是 COMMITTED 而提前返回），all_committed_match=false，说明广播并未修复不一致，同一实例在全集群存在两个不同的已提交命令。该观察覆盖本轮驱动的记录状态，未执行状态机，因此应用层后果仍是未决问题。
limitations: the already-committed record is prepared; the history that produced it (proposal, accept quorum, commit broadcast) is not constructed
the propagation property compares records, not applied state; executing the instances would be a separate observation
the third replica receives the instance only through the recoverer's Commit, so its record is not evidence about earlier rounds
the earlier artifacts' reviews remain valid for their own versions; this review covers the artifact that adds the propagation observation

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the obligation is that each field the recorder writes can be recovered at the offset where the writer placed it, and the predicate asserts bal_field_present on the header event; the retained run shows the header in hex with bal_field_present false, vbal_at_0 true, status_at_4 true and seq_at_5 true, so the derived boolean is checkable against the printed bytes and the printed written values. Entry and caller duty: the recorder runs only when Durable is true, which the harness sets and the prerequisite event reports together with the instance identity and the written field values; sync is called as the production callers do, and no other caller duty is needed for a record of one instance. Oracle: the comparison is against the value the harness asked the recorder to write, with distinct nonzero values so a default-zero buffer cannot pass by accident, and the deps region is left out of the comparison rather than silently assumed. Identity: the write-request prerequisite and the header event share instance 0.0, so the observation is correlated with the write it judges rather than with array order. Constructed input and legality: the claim's applicability is exactly a single recorder call with Durable true and distinct bal, vbal, Status and Seq, so a constructed instance is the full premise here; the alternative reading recorded in the claim (that the layout deliberately stores vbal in place of bal) is what a reviewer would have to accept to reject the finding, and the source shows both a bal write and a buffer sized 9+4N, which that reading would make vestigial. Observation path and completion: the harness writes, syncs, closes and reads the file back before emitting the event, so the observation completes without any wait, join or cleanup duty. Contrary evidence is reflected as limits rather than suppressed: no in-repository reader fixes the intended layout, the shipped run.go passes durable=false, and only one record is observed.
items.report_title: 稳定存储元数据记录丢失 bal 字段
items.report_answer: 启用 Durable 后，recordInstanceMetadata 产出的头部为 04030201|03|100f0e0d|deps：偏移 0 处是 vbal 的四个字节，写入的 bal 值不在记录中（bal_field_present=false），Status 落在第 4 字节、Seq 位于 [5:9)。该观察只针对一次真实写入所产出的记录，读取方缺失与默认配置 durable=false 属于限制而非本次判定的一部分。
limitations: no reader of the stable store exists in the snapshot, so the intended offsets are inferred from the recorder's own writes and buffer size
the shipped configuration passes durable=false, so this is an implementation-semantics defect rather than a live failure in the default deployment
only one instance and one record are observed; repeated records, the Deps region and partial writes are not compared

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.
items.report_title: 应用层不一致属性超出已接受义务范围
items.report_answer: 运行结果本身可复现：对端状态机读到 04，恢复者与第三副本读到 (void)，applied_match=false，即已提交记录的不一致确实进入了状态机。但已接受的义务 C1 在其 scope.excluded 中明确排除了 execution of the instance and client-visible replies，因此该属性断言的是范围之外事项，不能用来确认 C1；它需要作为独立义务（或经 F2/F3 扩展范围）重新固定。
counterevidence: the accepted claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector lists execution of the instance and client-visible replies under scope.excluded, so the applied-state property tests outside the accepted proposition (claim C1 scope, S20-exec)

the event is reproducible in the retained stream (applied_state_divergence with peer_value 04 and recoverer_value (void)), so the objection is about scope and attribution rather than about the observation (check 2f186bc17e13432fae3b653b42e46941)
limitations: the applied-state observation remains useful as construction knowledge and can be re-used by a new obligation whose scope includes applying the instance
the harness invokes Exec.executeCommand directly, so scheduling, watermarks and the recovery timeout are outside even the substituted execution path
the earlier artifacts and their reviews are unaffected; this review concerns only the artifact that adds the applied-state property

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: claim C3 requires that replicas holding the same instance committed apply the same effect for the instance's key, and the property asserts applied_match on the applied_state_divergence event; the retained run shows peer_value 04 against recoverer_value and third_value (void) with applied_match false, and the same event prints the command each replica held, so the applied difference is tied to the different committed vectors rather than to an unstated assumption. Entry and caller duties: the harness drives the recovery, the accept round and the Commit broadcast as before, then applies each record with Exec.executeCommand and probes the store with a GET command; the claim's scope now includes applying the instance and excludes the production loop, watermarks, timing and client-visible replies, and the harness substitutions are declared in the plan's semantic changes and uncertainties. Oracle and identity: the three printed values are read from each replica's replicated store for one key, the claim fixes the key as the one the committed commands touch, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so correlation is monotonic and the comparison is not derived from a context expected to change. Legal history: the committed records come from the same driven path as the confirmed C1 checks (recoverer and third replica NOOP, peer PUT), so the input is the observed consequence of the confirmed defect rather than a fabricated state. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the alternative reading that execution lies outside any obligation about adopting a value is exactly why this proposition is its own claim; the reservations that remain are recorded as limitations, namely direct execution instead of the production loop, one instance and one key, and the prepared committed record. The item therefore clears correspondence for C3 rather than extending C1.
items.report_title: 同一实例在不同副本产生不同的已应用效果
items.report_answer: 每个副本用自己的已提交记录执行后，对端状态机读到 04，而恢复者与第三副本读到 (void)，applied_match=false：同一实例在不同副本的状态机效果不同，说明记录层的不一致确实成为可观察的应用层分叉。该结论属于新义务 C3（其范围包含执行该实例），用于确认 C3；它不用于确认 C1。
limitations: the harness applies records directly with Exec.executeCommand, so scheduling, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are outside this check
one instance and one key are compared; other keys and repeated instances are not
the committed records are prepared/driven as in the C1 checks, so the history that produced them is not constructed

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicates: the three monitored properties encode the accepted C1 obligation and nothing else; the applied-state event is still printed by the harness but no monitor selects it, so the executed checker set matches the accepted scope exactly. Entry, schedule and completion: the harness is the reviewed driven version (Prepare/PrepareReply, the phase-1 restart's PreAccept and reply, the Accept and its reply, the Commit broadcast, with InstanceSpace re-read after every delivery), so the observations come from the records the handlers wrote. Oracle and identity: the same assertions and identity correlation as the reviewed three-property artifact, with the committed_reply prerequisite as admission alias for each monitor. Legal history: the prepared COMMITTED record and direct recovery entry remain declared in the claim scope. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the alternative that the applied-state observation should be confirmable under C1 is answered by claim C3, which owns that proposition and has its own reviewed check; the reservations that remain for this artifact are the ones already recorded (prepared committed record, substituted trigger) and are unchanged.
items.report_title: C1 检查集已仅含范围内属性
items.report_answer: 该工件执行的检查集只含三条范围内属性：解析处的采纳（adopted_committed=false）、恢复者与已提交副本的向量比较（vectors_match=false）、以及提交广播后三副本的一致性（all_committed_match=false）；应用层一致性不再由任何监控器选择，因此它不再进入 C1 的判定。三条属性与已复核的对应关系一致，前置条件、身份字段、法理与驱动轮次均未改变。
limitations: the harness still prints the applied-state event; only the monitor set excludes it, which is the point of this artifact
the prepared COMMITTED record and the direct recovery entry remain substitutions declared in the claim scope

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns must be processed without dereferencing absent bookkeeping and without terminating the replica; the predicate asserts panicked == false on the commit-result event, and the retained run reports panicked true with the panic value, plus no_effect true, so the assertion is evaluated on printed fields rather than inferred. Entry and message legality: the record is created by the real handlePreAccept for (Replica 0, Instance 0) at ballot 3 with one PUT command, which is what a recovery-led phase 1 sends to the owner, and the commit is a well-formed single NONE command at ballot 4 with matching replica and instance, which is what the recoverer broadcasts after restarting phase 1 with NOOP; both are protocol messages, so the history is legal for a replica that no longer holds the instance in memory. Oracle and the recover() wrapper: the harness wraps only the delivery in recover so a panic is reported as an event instead of killing the test process; the handler itself is unmodified, and the wrapper is what makes the panic observable rather than what creates it, which the printed panic value confirms. Identity: the prerequisite record event and the commit-result event share instance 0.0, so the observation is tied to the record under test. Inference to termination: the run loop dispatches handlers directly in its select statement with no recover, so a panic in handleCommit propagates out of the loop and ends the process; that step is a source-based inference and is recorded as a limitation rather than as an observed process exit, because the harness does not drive the loop. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the alternative reading that such a record can never belong to the owner is contradicted by the message-created record, and the remaining reservations (dispatcher not modelled, single instance, no history) are recorded as limitations. The item therefore clears correspondence for C4 while keeping the inference boundary explicit.
items.report_title: NOOP 提交使实例所有者空指针崩溃
items.report_answer: 由消息创建记录（无 leader bookkeeping）的实例所有者收到一条合法的单 NONE 命令 Commit 后，handleCommit 在重提议分支解引用 inst.lb.clientProposals 触发空指针 panic（事件 panic_value 为 invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference），且该提交未生效（no_effect=true）。运行循环对该处理器没有 recover，因此该 panic 会终止副本进程；这一推断属于限制说明，harness 只观察到 panic 本身。
limitations: the harness observes the panic, not the replica process terminating; the termination step follows from the run loop having no recover and is an inference
the history that would make a recovery-led PreAccept reach a restarted owner is not constructed; the check fixes the two messages and the record state
the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery is a separate question and is not part of this check
